text:
ana: quick note — noticed p99 for /v1/generate jumped ~40% on the dashboard after last night's routing tweak. dashboard shows p50/p95 stable tho.

jordan: ugh. which dashboard? the per-endpoint rollup or the route split view?

ana: per-endpoint rollup (console -> endpoints -> /v1/generate). p99 moved from ~420ms to ~620ms, p95 unchanged.

priya: is this the same signal that's used for SLAs? wondering if it's a sampling artifact.

morgan: i dug in fast: raw telemetry (trace store) still shows p99 ~430ms. the rollup is based on sampled metrics from the routing layer. looks like some requests lost their "route" tag after fallback to the cheap-pool.

ana: that would explain it — rollup aggregates by endpoint but if route tag dropped, those fallbacks end up in a different bucket and blow up percentiles when merged.

jordan: do we know why tags were dropped? the routing change added route-weight sampling to reduce cardinality. maybe bug in the sampling filter.

morgan: yep. sampling filter was applied before we copy over route metadata for fallback paths. we should have applied it after. simple ordering bug.

ops-bot: deploy 3045670000 to routing-service succeeded (canary: 3/5 nodes).

priya: can we hotfix to preserve route metadata during sampling? also: console should surface sample counts so p99 with low effective sample isn't misleading.

theo: agree on sample counts. proposal: show sample_count and sampled_percent next to p50/p95/p99 and render a yellow warn if sampled_percent < 50%.

jordan: small API debate: do we expose `sampled_percent` on metrics API or add it to the endpoint metadata? i'd prefer it in the metrics response so the UI can render it without extra joins.

sam: from infra side, adding it to metrics response is cheaper (single query). but telemetry team prefers normalizing as a tag for downstream rollups.

priya: another UX ask: add a tooltip explaining that p99 may be derived from sampled rollups and link to the raw-trace p99 for verification. we keep sending users to raw data when in doubt.

morgan: hotfix queued — reorder sampling -> tag-copy -> sampling-apply. prepping patch now. will push to canary then global.

ana: timeline? ops-bot says canary was 3/5 nodes. we should block global until patch lands.

morgan: plan: push patch to canary in 15m, let it run for 30m, then roll.

jordan: also need a PR to console: add sample_count column and warning state. small front-end CL, will draft.

priya: also confirm that rollup merge semantics treat missing route as a separate null tag, not as "unknown route" that gets merged into /v1/generate. i've seen merges that artificially aggregate nulls into the main bucket.

morgan: yes, currently null tags are merged under "route:unknown" and show up in endpoint totals. we should instead keep unknown separate and not use it in p99 rollups unless explicitly requested.

theo: we should add automated alerting for % of requests with missing route tag > 1% over 5m. that would have caught this during canary.

sam: agreed — created alert ticket INF-4821.

ana: thanks all. after hotfix and console warn, can we also add a short blurb in the release notes so customers understand the transient p99 drift?

jordan: yes — i'll add a note under "telemetry/metrics" that we fixed route tag preservations and updated UI to show sample counts.

morgan: pushing canary patch now. will update thread with canary metrics.

ops-bot: deploy 3045679001 to routing-service (canary) succeeded.

morgan: canary looks good — sample_missing_rate dropped from 2.7% to 0.1% on the patched nodes. raw and rollup p99 aligned again.

ana: awesome. leaving this open until console CL and alert are merged. :thumbsup:

jordan: opened console PR #1248 — adds sample_count column + tooltip.

priya: filing a short playbook entry: "If p99 spikes without p95 change — check sample counts, missing route tags, and route-level fallbacks."

ana: perfect. closing loop in 48hrs after monitoring.

sam: note -> long term: consider propagating `route_id` as part of trace baggage so future sampling can be route-aware without brittle ordering.

morgan: agreed, adding follow-up RFC.

ana: thanks everyone.
